detailed_results.feedback: The student effectively articulates two significant new learnings: the practical application of carbon emission scopes and the detailed process and significance of B-Corp certification. The explanation goes beyond mere definitions to highlight the practical insights gained.
citations: In this internship, I learned the specific strategies businesses use to identify and mitigate their emissions depending on where they are in the value chain.
So I went from learning how they get produced → how to reduce their carbon footprint depending on the specific practice.
This summer , I assisted in Bonduelle Americas ' recertification for B-Corp, as they need to go through recertification every 4 years.
being able to see how specifically B-Corp grades organizations on their practices and what kind of data companies need to provide in order to prove their compliance was eye-opening.

detailed_results.feedback: The student identifies two distinct surprises: the unexpectedly high volume of water used by companies and the challenges of internal corporate communication. Both are well-explained and reflect genuine observations from the internship.
citations: One thing that surprised me is how many gallons of water companies use. For some reason, it never occurred to me that companies used millions of gallons a week.
The second thing for me was how difficult company communication can be.
it took a long time to hear back from other associates to respond to my emails, if at all.

detailed_results.feedback: This section is outstanding. The student clearly articulates how their internship experience bridges the gap between scientific understanding and business strategy, providing a compelling narrative for interviews. The specific example of heat waves impacting food manufacturing demonstrates a sophisticated understanding of real-world business risks.
citations: I plan to position myself as someone who brings both a scientific foundation in environmental studies and the ability to translate that knowledge into business strategy.

Before this internship, I primarily understood climate change through a research and technical lens... Through my ESG internship at Bonduelle, I developed the ability to apply these learnings directly to real-world business operations and risks.

For example, I analyzed how increasing heat waves in Georgia put stress on aging power grids, leading to more frequent blackouts. In a food manufacturing context, this means halted production, product spoilage when refrigeration fails, and ultimately financial losses.

What I’ve learned to do well is bridge the gap between science and business: identifying where climate risks intersect with operational challenges, and then framing them in a way that companies can act on.

the advantage that Bondulle has is that a lot of its competitors are not B-Corp certified.
